Pilot next steps and commercial terms
transcript:
Meeting: 2026-04-14 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET | Duration ~56m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (BlueHarbor Head of ML), Ethan Ross (Platform Eng), Lina Gomez (CISO)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this light but make sure we cover capacity for your upcoming campaign and double check the security asks. Can everyone hear ok?
[00:09] Maya: Yep, loud and clear. We've got about 12 minutes blocked after for ops follow up but otherwise good.
[00:16] Diego: quick intro from me too, I'm the SE that will help with the smoke tests and perf tuning.
[00:21] Ethan: Great. Quick context — we saw a 3x jump in inference requests during last holiday and want to avoid outages this year.
[00:29] Lina: also need to validate encryption in transit+at rest and that we can integrate with our HSM. SOC two questions too.
[00:36] Avery: understood. For capacity, we suggested a dedicated pool with burst capacity and autoscale policy — Diego, can you summarize the numbers?
[00:44] Diego: Sure. Based on the sample traces Maya sent last quarter — which thanks for sending — we're projecting steady-state 600 rps with spikes to 2.2k rps for short windows. For gen-heavy endpoints (context windows ~1k tokens) we'd recommend reserving 8 x A100 equivalent instances and a burst buffer of another 4 for short bursts; effective throughput depends on batching and sequence length.
[01:10] Maya: That sounds reasonable. A couple clarifications: are those raw GPU counts or instances behind the autoscaler? How quickly does the burst provision?
[01:18] Diego: they're instance-equivalents in the dedicated pool. Burst is pre-warmed capacity we can carve out — it can be available in under a minute for short bursts because we keep a small hot pool; if you want instant unlimited burst we can discuss overprovisioning but that's expensive.
[01:31] Ethan: Minute is fine, but we need to avoid cold starts for latency-critical flows. What's the expected p95 added latency on swap-in?
[01:38] Diego: In tests, swap-in latency was 180–350ms depending on model size and KV warmup; with prefix caching and warm KV we can cut that significantly.
[01:46] Maya: about prefix caching — we run a lot of repeated system prompts and product descriptions, would prefix caching help?
[01:52] Diego: Absolutely. Prefix/KV caching could drop token compute for repeated prefixes by around 40–60% depending on hit rate. We'll need the prompt set to recommend eviction policies.
[02:04] Lina: on security — we require SAML SSO, RBAC scoped to routes, audit logs retained 2 years, and HSM-backed keywrap for model keys. Is that in scope for the private control plane or hosted?
[02:16] Avery: Good question. For hosted we offer tenant-level KMS integration; for Private (VPC) we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and longer audit retention. Diego, correct me if I'm wrong on exact limits.
[02:25] Diego: Yep. On Hosted we can integrate with an external KMS via API for envelope keys, but HSM direct attachments are only available with Private deployments. SOC2 controls and 2-year log retention are part of the enterprise compliance add-on.
[02:37] Lina: So to meet our procurement, we'd likely need the Private deployment? Or could we do a pilot on hosted then move to Private before contract?
[02:46] Avery: Typical path is pilot on dedicated hosted with strict access controls and then migrate to Private for production. We can include a transition plan and migration checklist in the SOW.
[02:54] Ethan: On observability — we need per-route token breakdowns and traces we can correlate with our APM (we use Datadog). Can Redwood export spans?
[03:02] Diego: Yes — we can emit OpenTelemetry spans and token-level metrics to a push endpoint. We'll send an example mapping file.
[03:09] Maya: great, please include sample dashboards for cost per route, and a breakdown for embeddings vs gen.
[03:15] Diego: noted. We'll also include an example of the auto-pan policy if a model regression is detected so you can rollback automatically.
[03:22] Avery: shifting to economics — we proposed a 3-month pilot with usage commitment. For the pilot we can offer a 20% pilot discount plus burst credits. After pilot we can discuss a month-to-month or reserved capacity commitment.
[03:34] Maya: what's the unit economics for gen token cost versus embeddings in the proposed config? Our embedding usage is high but predictable.
[03:41] Avery: embeddings are about 0.2x cost per token vs generation; exact numbers in the sheet I'll send. Diego, maybe run a back-of-envelope for their mix?
[03:49] Diego: based on the telemetry we saw, embeddings are ~40% of requests but only 10% of token volume; generation dominates token spend. We can optimize embeddings by batching and caching too.
[03:58] Ethan: a practical question — what quantization options do you support for our larger models? We need to balance latency vs hallucination risk.
[04:06] Diego: We support INT8 and some Q4 variants; quantization reduces memory and can increase throughput but may slightly affect quality. We'd recommend running an eval with your prompts — we'll help with an eval harness to measure quality regressions.
[04:19] Maya: yes please, we have a small evaluation set (~150 prompts) for this purpose.
[04:24] Lina: procurement will also ask about subcontractors and where logs are stored — data residency is a requirement for some PII in EU customers.
[04:32] Avery: noted — Redwood has EU regions and can pin data residency per account in Private. We'll surface the compliance deck.
[04:38] Maya: quick follow-up — during last flash event our error rate spiked due to throttling at the control plane. Any plans to mitigate that?
[04:46] Diego: We're adding a control-plane fallback route that will be in canary soon; for dedicated customers we provide an autonomous fallback policy that switches to a lighter model variant in the same pool if the primary capacity is saturated. That lowers quality slightly but keeps latency and availability.
[04:59] Ethan: How is canary rollout handled? We need to test model changes without global impact.
[05:04] Diego: Our console supports canary by percent and route, with automatic rollback based on latency/error thresholds. We can create a canary for BlueHarbor's top three routes.
[05:12] Avery: okay to pivot to operational plan — proposed timeline: week 1 (now) exchange prompts + telemetry, week 2 run smoke tests, week 3 pilot kickoff with pre-warmed burst and observability, week 7 assess and decide on Private migration.
[05:26] Maya: timeline looks good; we need internal approval from procurement and security.
[05:31] Lina: procurement will need an inventory of third-party subprocessors and the SOC2 report; also details on audit log export and retention.
[05:40] Avery: I'll attach the SOC2 summary and subprocessors list. We also have a private compliance packet for Private deployments.
[05:46] Ethan: small note — for the smoke test please keep traces anonymized; we can't send raw PII.
[05:51] Diego: understood, we'll accept sampled telemetry and synthetic prompts if needed.
[05:56] Maya: one more operational ask — can we get a per-route cost forecast with 95th percentile and a worst-case spike scenario? That'll help procurement.
[06:05] Avery: we'll produce a forecast spreadsheet with steady state, 95th, and spike estimates and include the pilot discount math.
[06:12] Lina: anything about legal around indemnities we should flag now?
[06:18] Avery: high level no but we'll mark the standard SLAs and any add-on compliance clauses. Legal will review the SOW draft once we have numbers.
[06:25] Ethan: sounds good.
[06:28] Avery: ok let's recap actions and owners. Diego will run the smoke test and share spans; Maya will provide prompts and distribution; Lina will send KMS/HSM and retention details; I'll send commercial and compliance docs.
[06:40] Maya: thanks everyone.
[06:42] Lina: thanks.
[06:44] End meeting.
